data.name: Aqif
data.gender_notes: Aqif is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.short_meaning: The one who keeps awake (for prayer)
data.long_meaning: In Arabic, Aqif means 'the one who keeps awake'. This name is derived from the Quranic verse, 'And keep up prayer and give zakat and hold in honour the bond of Allah.' (Surah Al-Baqarah, 2:231). The one who keeps awake for prayer is someone who is conscious of Allah and is always ready to answer His call. The name Aqif carries the meaning “The one who keeps awake (for prayer)” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Aqif usually hope their child will grow to embody the one who keeps awake (for prayer) and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name for a conscious and devoted servant of Allah
data.etymology: Aqif belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “The one who keeps awake (for prayer).”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Aqif total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Ibn al-Jawzi (d. 1200 CE) The name Aqif carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: In his book 'al-Mawduıat wa al-Tawheed' (The Unique and the Divine), Ibn al-Jawzi mentioned a man named 'Aqif ibn Aws Thaqafi, who was a poet and a student of Imam al-Shafiıi (d. 820 CE). This 'Aqif is also known for his debates with the Muħtazila scholars, particularly al-Jahiz and al-Nafs al-Zaki. He was a strong defender of orthodox Sunni theology and opposed the Muħtazila doctrines, which were seen as deviating from the traditional Islamic beliefs.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Ibn Abd al-Hadid (d. 1252 CE) The name Aqif carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: In his work 'Sharh Nahj al-Balagha' (Commentary on the Sayings of the Prophet), Ibn Abd al-Hadid mentioned a scholar named 'Aqif ibn Makram, who was a companion of Imam Malik ibn Anas (d. 795 CE) and one of the earliest scholars of the Maliki school of law. He is known for his commentary on 'Sahifat al-Siddiq' (Letter of Ali) and his work on the biographies of the Prophet's companions. 'Aqif was a prominent figure in the early development of the Maliki school and played a significant role in codifying its legal principles.
